title: Suggestions for review — nothing here is implemented on your behalf
description: Every suggestion is a proposal with an owner-side decision field still open. Priority is ordered by how many blocked questions it unblocks, not by how attractive it sounds. Where a suggestion would require buying something, changing a policy, or touching another session's files, that is stated in the dependency column instead of quietly done.
decision_rule: Owner sets decision to ACCEPT, REJECT or DEFER (with a note). An open decision means no code or configuration change is made on the strength of the suggestion alone.

rows.suggestion: Buy a licensed historical NFL lines dataset (openers plus closers, point-in-time) before building any further model machinery.
rows.rationale: Six of the fifteen blocking questions (backtest, CLV, correlation against market price, hold, settlement parity, live-versus-pre-game scope) are all variants of the same missing input. The league's own betting data is exclusively distributed, so there is no official free path to it; every alternative is a licence question.
rows.risk: Licence terms may forbid storing or republishing derived numbers, which would constrain what this site can show; and a low-quality line history quietly poisons every backtest, so the vendor's point-in-time guarantees matter more than coverage breadth.

rows.suggestion: Originate the game total first, and derive the spread from the two scoring intensities rather than modelling the margin directly.
rows.rationale: Scoring totals are the more stable primitive and the published evidence of mispricing clusters in totals (quadratic relationship to closing line, streak effects) and in prior-record overreaction, which is easier to exploit with a scoring model than a margin model.
rows.risk: Spread then inherits every totals error twice over, so a wrong total produces two wrong numbers and a correlated pair of bets that look like two positions.

rows.suggestion: Run one full season in paper mode with the published gate set before any capital, and treat that season as the competition's first cohort.
rows.rationale: The sample required to distinguish a 55% hit rate from break-even is about 2,243 settled bets, and at 150 bets a season the provable floor is roughly 62.4%; a selective strategy therefore needs multi-season validation before anyone funds it. Paper mode converts that uncomfortable arithmetic into a schedule instead of a loss.
rows.risk: Paper discipline overstates real execution quality (limits, repricing, voids), which is itself a reason to log every simulated slip and compare it to the posted line at that second.
rows.dependency: Owner: accept that v1 earns nothing.

rows.suggestion: Make abstention a first-class output: publish 'no position' as a decision with a reason, and enforce one edge threshold globally.
rows.rationale: Selectivity is the only lever that converts a marginal edge into a detectable one, because it raises mean edge per bet faster than it raises sample. A system that always finds a bet is a system that always pays the vig.
rows.risk: Long dry spells feel like a broken system; the dashboard must show the abstain rate and its rationale or the operator will override it.

rows.suggestion: Score the leaderboard on the 95% lower confidence bound of expected value (with a multiple-testing deflator), never on profit, ROI or rank of PnL.
rows.rationale: Raw PnL is exactly the luck metric the brief asks us to remove. Ranking on a confidence bound is the standard correction for the winner's curse when many candidates are screened, and the forecasting literature has a purpose-built version of it.
rows.risk: Almost everything will fail. That is the point, but it changes the culture of the competition from 'find a winner each week' to 'survive a season of audits'.
rows.dependency: None — we have implemented the statistic; adoption is the decision.

rows.suggestion: Refuse to model parlays as products of singles; publish a correlation-adjusted parlay value tool that shows the correction size next to the price.
rows.rationale: Correlated legs are permitted only inside Same Game Parlays, are repriced when a leg voids, and parlay-card hold is audited as its own category — three independent signs that combined prices embed correlation and a wider margin. Presenting a naive product as 'value' is the most reliable way to lose money with confidence.
rows.risk: Our joint model may disagree with the operator's correlation, in which case our 'edge' is model error, not mispricing — which is why the tool must display both prices side by side.

rows.suggestion: Treat the change in the injury report as the signal, not the level, and store every report snapshot with its capture timestamp.
rows.rationale: The official file is a per-day practice participation record with a game-status layer, and club documents explicitly mark status changes; the market reprices on the delta. A level-based model double-counts chronic cases and misses the one line that moved.
rows.risk: Snapshot discipline is unforgiving: if a capture fails, the diff for that week is silently lost, so the collector must alert on a missing expected report rather than just on an error.
rows.dependency: Needs a host to run on (Q-19).

rows.suggestion: Build the Next-Man-Up deficiency index from official roster mechanics rather than from scraped depth charts.
rows.rationale: The rules tell us exactly how many replacements a club may elevate and who is eligible; the injury report tells us who is unavailable. Together they bound the replacement set without depending on 32 separately designed club pages, and the expected-vs-replacement gap is then something we can estimate and own.
rows.risk: Eligibility is not intent: a club may dress a rookie it never uses, so the index must be calibrated by actual snap share, not by roster order.

rows.suggestion: Use the free state-regulator machine-readable reports to calibrate hold by market family, instead of quoting industry folklore.
rows.rationale: Illinois publishes monthly sports wagering detail with a matching CSV and a Sport Detail report; New York publishes statewide and per-operator weekly and monthly Excel; Nevada requires books to keep win-to-write percentages per sport and for parlay cards. That is an auditable, official basis for the single most important assumption in the model — the vig.
rows.risk: State-level aggregates are not market-level margins, and publication lags by about a month, so this calibrates priors, it does not price a game.

rows.suggestion: Make the league's prohibited-wager classes a hard, tested gate in the bet-generation path, not a policy document.
rows.rationale: The league publishes four categories (injury-based, officiating-based, determinable by one person in one play, pre-determined) and asks operators not to offer them. Any strategy library that can emit such a bet is a liability in code review, whatever its expected value.
rows.risk: Over-blocking: an injury-derived feature used to price a legal total is fine, so the gate must test the market's subject, never the model's inputs.
rows.dependency: None — implemented in engine/compliance.py, needs adoption.

rows.suggestion: Seal leaderboard entries: submit a hash of code plus config plus data snapshot before the season, publish ranks only from settled, official results.
rows.rationale: The difference between a research notebook and a competition is that the competition cannot be edited after the outcome. Content-addressed entries also make the multiple-comparison correction honest, because we know exactly how many candidates were tried.
rows.risk: Disputes about what the hash covers; mitigate by publishing the hashing recipe in the repo.

rows.suggestion: Keep a public graveyard of killed strategies, with the gate they failed, and forbid re-submission without a stated change.
rows.rationale: Most of the cost in a strategy programme is re-testing the same attractive-but-dead idea under a new name. A graveyard converts that waste into a memory, and gives the multiple-testing correction a real denominator.
rows.risk: People will route around it by renaming; the deduplication test in the leaderboard engine must therefore be content-based, not label-based.

rows.suggestion: Generate the weekly executive summary from the data registers automatically, and let the only human act be approve or intervene.
rows.rationale: The brief asks for no manual input from you. A summary written by hand drifts from the data it summarises; one rendered from the same JSON cannot, and every number in it inherits a source link by construction.
rows.risk: Auto-generation can also make a bad week look tidy, so the summary must lead with the failed gates rather than the wins.
rows.no_source_reason: Internal proposal derived from the project's own state; the evidence behind it is cited in the rows it references.

rows.suggestion: Do not build a weather feature until its source, granularity and lag are verified; today it is a gap, not a feature.
rows.rationale: The published evidence that precipitation interacts with favourite-underdog profitability is exactly the kind of single-paper result that dies on replication, and a weather input smuggled in from an unverified source would contaminate a table the site promises is sourced.
rows.risk: The temptation to bolt on a plausible-sounding adjustment is how models become un-auditable.

rows.suggestion: Drop referee-crew and officiating features from the roadmap for v1.
rows.rationale: They point at a market class the league prohibits, and there is no official published assignment feed we could cite. Two reasons to spend nothing there.
rows.risk: If a competitor exploits it, our totals will be slightly worse on some games; we judge that acceptable against the compliance and sourcing cost.

rows.suggestion: Adopt the site's own tables as the single source of truth: no number may exist in prose, a slide, or a chat that is not generated from a register row.
rows.rationale: This is the only structural defence against the failure the brief is worried about — a plausible figure appearing somewhere and acquiring authority. The build already fails a row that lacks a source, so extending the rule to prose costs nothing.
rows.risk: Prose becomes drier and every claim needs an id. That is the intended side effect.
rows.no_source_reason: Internal proposal derived from the project's own state; the evidence behind it is cited in the rows it references.

rows.suggestion: Add an explicit automation ledger so 'no manual input' is a claim we can audit: what runs, where, when, and what it did last time.
rows.rationale: Unattended pipelines fail quietly, and a dashboard nobody refreshed is more dangerous than no dashboard. A last-run timestamp on every table turns silent failure into a visible one — which is why each page already prints its as-of date.
rows.risk: Requires a host and one alert channel (Q-19); without them this suggestion is decoration.
rows.no_source_reason: Internal proposal derived from the project's own state; the evidence behind it is cited in the rows it references.

rows.suggestion: Give the four sessions one non-overlapping file split and one integrator, and write it into COORDINATION.md before anyone else builds a second site.
rows.rationale: The remote shows four branches from the same base, three of them claiming the identical scope including docs/. Independent claims produce duplicate artefacts and merge pain, which is precisely what the coordination protocol in the brief exists to prevent.
rows.risk: Another session may already be integrating; the protocol's stale-claim rule (60 minutes without commits) plus union-merging of files is the safest reconciliation.
rows.dependency: All sessions; recorded by this session.

rows.suggestion: Borrow banking-style model risk governance: independent validation, a model card per strategy, and annual re-approval.
rows.rationale: The discipline that makes a model trustworthy is that someone who did not build it tries to break it. Our gates are the validation; the model card is what makes it reviewable; the graveyard is the audit trail.
rows.risk: Process weight on a small operation; keep it to one card per strategy, auto-filled.

rows.suggestion: Publish the detectable-edge curve (sample per season versus required true edge) on the leaderboard and validation pages.
rows.rationale: It converts 'remove luck from the equation' from a slogan into a number every entrant can see before entering, and it is the honest answer to why most claimed edges are unprovable at our volume.
rows.risk: It will discourage entries. Correctly.

rows.suggestion: Keep live and in-play betting out of v1 entirely.
rows.rationale: In-play data, low-latency video and the official feed all sit behind one exclusive distributor, the hold is widest live, and our inputs (availability, rest, weather) are pre-game by nature. The only honest in-play edge would be latency, which is infrastructure we are not building.
rows.risk: Concedes a market family where soft lines genuinely exist.

rows.suggestion: Set the kill criteria before the first stake, and hold them: pre-registered demotion thresholds, weekly review, no discretionary rescue.
rows.rationale: The cheapest way to lose money with a good model is to keep funding it through a bad run because next month looks like the turn. A pre-committed rule is the only defence that survives the moment it is needed.
rows.risk: A real edge can be killed inside its normal variance band; mitigate by requiring the lower bound to breach, not the point estimate.

rows.suggestion: Put a responsible-gambling block and a plain statement of expected loss in the site footer and the staking output.
rows.rationale: This is a tool that helps someone stake money on uncertain outcomes. The league's own framework pairs betting access with mandatory responsible-gambling investment and a helpline referral, and state regulators link the same helpline from their own pages. Copying that posture costs nothing and omitting it is a foreseeable harm.
rows.risk: None worth naming.
rows.dependency: None — implemented in the site footer.

rows.suggestion: Do not let the leaderboard's rewards create an incentive to overfit: pay for measured, gated skill only, and never for a single-season return.
rows.rationale: A prize for the highest raw return is a prize for variance, and rational entrants will respond by taking more variance — the opposite of the brief's intent. Tying rewards to gate passage plus confidence-bound EV makes the winning behaviour the behaviour we want.
rows.risk: Fewer, duller entries; and any cash prize reintroduces the legal question in Q-13, so keep rewards non-cash until counsel answers.
